decks.name: LeetCode #133 - Clone Graph
decks.description: Create a deep copy of an undirected connected graph where each node contains a value and a list of neighbors

cards.question: Clone Graph: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy (clone) of the graph. Each node in the graph contains a value (int) and a list (List[Node]) of its neighbors. The graph is represented using adjacency list where adj[i] contains all nodes that are directly connected to node i.

solutions.name: Depth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use DFS with hash map to clone graph while avoiding infinite loops. Create hash map oldToNew to track original nodes to their clones. DFS function takes a node, checks if already cloned (in hash map), returns existing clone if found. Otherwise, create new node with same value, store in hash map, then recursively clone all neighbors and add to clone's neighbor list. This ensures each node is cloned exactly once. Base case handles already-visited nodes by returning cached clone. Handle edge case of empty graph by checking if input node is None. Time O(V+E) visiting all vertices and edges. Space O(V) for hash map storing all cloned nodes.

solutions.timeDescription: We visit each vertex (node) exactly once and traverse each edge twice (once from each endpoint), where V is number of vertices and E is number of edges in the graph
solutions.spaceDescription: Hash map stores one entry per vertex. Recursion stack depth is bounded by number of vertices in worst case of linear graph
solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given graph with node 1 connected to [2,4], node 2 connected to [1,3], node 3 connected to [2,4], node 4 connected to [1,3]: Start DFS at node 1, create clone of node 1, store in map. Process neighbor 2: not in map, create clone of node 2, store in map. Process neighbor 1 of node 2: already in map, return cached clone. Process neighbor 3 of node 2: not in map, create clone of node 3. Continue recursively until all nodes cloned. Return clone of original node 1.

solutions.name: Breadth First Search
solutions.explanation: Use BFS with hash map and queue to clone graph level by level. First handle edge case of empty graph. Create hash map oldToNew, clone starting node and add to map. Initialize queue with original starting node. Process queue: dequeue current node, iterate through its neighbors. For each neighbor, if not yet cloned, create clone and add to map, enqueue original neighbor. Add cloned neighbor to current clone's neighbor list. This processes graph level by level, ensuring each node cloned exactly once. Return clone of starting node from hash map. Time O(V+E) visiting all vertices and edges. Space O(V) for hash map and queue.
